title: M’laya ropeway standoff: JAC hesitant to attend minister’s stakeholder meet

ai.summary: Women-led groups in Meghalaya have maintained a peaceful sit-in protest for five days outside a statue in Shillong, demanding the government abandon a Rs 151 crore ropeway project that threatens water sources. The Joint Action Committee (JAC) stated it will continue the agitation until the project is scrapped, despite Cabinet Minister Sanbor Shullai convening a meeting to discuss implementation.

facts.claim: The anti-ropeway demonstration entered its fifth day
facts.quote: The anti-ropeway demonstration entered its fifth day on Tuesday as women-led groups maintained their peaceful protest outside the U Kiang Nangbah statue in the state capital.

facts.claim: The project is funded by the New Development Bank and the Central Government under the PM-DevINE scheme
facts.quote: The project, which features a 913-metre ropeway line funded by the New Development Bank and the Central Government under the PM-DevINE scheme, is designed to utilise a monocable gondola configuration connecting Madan Laban to an upper terminal near the Shillong Viewpoint.

facts.claim: The JAC stated it will continue the sit-in until the project is scrapped
facts.quote: The Joint Action Committee (JAC) on Tuesday reiterated that its indefinite sit-in will continue until the Meghalaya government completely abandons the Rs 151 crore Shillong ropeway project.

facts.claim: The JAC General Secretary, Dr. Linda Marbaniang, stated the project poses a direct threat to water sources
facts.quote: Marbaniang reiterated the committee’s resolve to continue with the peaceful agitation until the project is scrapped, maintaining that the venture poses a direct threat to the vital water sources and catchment areas of U Lum Shyllong.

facts.claim: Cabinet Minister Sanbor Shullai convened a meeting on Wednesday to discuss implementation
facts.quote: Cabinet Minister Sanbor Shullai has convened a meeting on Wednesday with local stakeholders to deliberate on the proposed ropeway venture.

facts.claim: Tourism Minister Paul Lyngdoh ruled out rolling back the project
facts.quote: Last week, Tourism Minister Paul Lyngdoh had ruled out rolling back the Shillong Ropeway project, stating that it has secured all mandatory environmental clearances.

ai.background_note: The Meghalaya government faces pressure to abandon a Rs 151 crore ropeway project that activists claim threatens water sources, despite the project having secured environmental clearances.
